properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 8:07PM MDT until October 23 at 10:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding along the Conejos River and its tributaries will
continue in and around the communities of Conejos and Antonito due
to excessive rainfall over the previous couple days.

* WHERE...Southeastern Conejos County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 1015 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Conejos River, area creeks, streams, and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.
Mandatory evacuations continue along the Conejos River near
Antonito. Streams continue to rise due to excess runoff from
earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 800 PM MDT, emergency management reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring.
- Stream gauges on the Conejos River and San Antonio River near
Manassa continue to show rising water.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Manassa, Sanford, Antonito, Romeo, Conejos, Bountiful and Ortiz.
- Highway 17 between Antonito and Cumbres Pass remains closed due
to reported water and debris over the roadway.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
SVRABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
South Central Santa Fe County in north central New Mexico...

* Until 830 PM MDT.

* At 805 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Stanley, or 8
miles northeast of Moriarty, moving northeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Stanley.
properties.instruction:

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and nickel size hail.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 7:54PM MDT until October 23 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 1100 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 754 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Up to 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Additional rainfall of up to 0.25 inches is expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Timberon, Sacramento, Weed, Hay Canyon, Cox Canyon and Surveyors
Canyon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 PM MDT THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 9:53PM EDT until October 24 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents expected. Strong north to south longshore
current expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Georgetown County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM to 9 AM EDT
Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM EDT
Saturday through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Vulnerable causeways to and from local beaches may
experience minor coastal flooding. Low-lying roads and
locations along the Intracoastal Waterway and adjacent tidal
creeks may observe minor coastal flooding. Check with local
officials for the latest information regarding coastal flood
impacts and closures. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 5 AM TO 9 AM EDT SATURDAY... ...HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 6 AM EDT SATURDAY THROUGH SATURDAY EVENING

properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Dona Ana County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 1100 PM MDT.

* At 753 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Santa Teresa, Vado, Berino, Chamberino, La Union, San Miguel,
Mesquite, La Mesa, Union Pacific Intermodal Terminal and High
Valley.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 7:41PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms will continue this evening, with
activity redeveloping again in the afternoon Saturday and
persisting into Saturday evening. Recent wildfire burn scars in
Lincoln County remain vulnerable to abrupt runoff and flash
flooding. While individual showers and thunderstorms will
typically produce rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inch, multiple
rounds of storms will increase the risk of flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, dense fog will reduce

south winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt and waves 3 to 6
ft expected.

to Sheboygan.

* WHEN...For the Dense Fog Advisory, until 10 AM CDT Saturday.

vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

If you must navigate, proceed with caution. Use proper fog
signals. Make sure all running lights are on. Remember to use
your radar and compass.
